To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the stereo bird's eye feature volume, which is the projection of stereo features to the bird eye view coordinates, is a good representation for layout estimation, (b) the inverse perspective mapping features are useful for layout estimation, and (c) a combination of the two is better than either one alone.

(i) a good internal representation of the stereo images is essential for layout prediction, (ii) the bird's eye features are more important than the stereo features, (iii) using the IPM as supervisory signal can help improve the performance.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of end-to-end learning of bird's eye representation for accurate layout estimation.
developing a novel end-to-end deep learning network to estimate accurate bird's eye view layouts.

the following contributions: (i) we propose a new end-to-end supervised deep learning framework for stereo bird's eye layout estimation, (ii) we demonstrate that our approach outperforms the state-of-the-arts on two datasets and (iii) we show that accurate stereo depth estimation is neither necessary nor sufficient for layout estimation and that learning a good representation is crucial for layout estimation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SBEVNet outperforms other baselines by 3-5% on KITTI dataset, while on the CARLA dataset the performance improvement is even more significant, 5-10%.
the proposed SBEVNet framework can learn the bird's eye representation from stereo images and use it to estimate the bird's eye semantic map, which is a crucial step towards autonomous driving.
our network is able to learn to extract bird's eye view features from the stereo images and use them for accurate bird's eye view map estimation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present an end-to-end deep network for BEV layout estimation which is capable of learning a good internal BEV representation from stereo images.

SBEVNet learns the internal representation of the bird's eye features which are capable of reasoning the spatial layout of the scene and hence can outperform the baselines which are based on the disparity volume alone.
we show how to learn the bird's eye representation for the stereo images in an end-to-end manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
accurate depth estimation from stereo images is not sufficient to obtain accurate layout estimation.
the network can learn to reason over the spatial layout of the scene without the need of explicit supervision.
accurate depth estimation may not always be required for solving certain computer vision problems.
